The Gershonites were one of the three main divisions of the Levites, along with the Kohathites and Merarites (Numbers 3:17; 1 Chronicles 6:1). 

During the wilderness wanderings, the Gershonites were responsible for the tabernacle curtains, coverings, screens, and related duties (Numbers 3:25). They were counted in the census of the Levites (Numbers 3:22) and were given wagons and oxen to transport their assigned parts of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:7). 

In the division of the Promised Land, the Gershonites were allocated thirteen cities across the territories of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and eastern Manasseh (Joshua 21:6; 1 Chronicles 6:62). Notable Gershonites include Asaph, a prominent musician and psalmist in King David's court (1 Chronicles 6:39), and Jahath, a Levite leader during the reign of King Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 29:12). 

The Gershonites played a significant role in the transportation, setup, and maintenance of the tabernacle, and later in the music and worship of the temple. Their dedicated service, along with that of the other Levite clans, was essential to the proper functioning of Israel's religious life.

name: Kohath
title: Son of Levi; Levite clan ancestor
bio: Kohath was the second son of Levi and grandson of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Genesis 46:11). He went to Egypt with Jacob's household (Genesis 46:11) and his descendants were counted in the census of Israel (Exodus 6:16; Numbers 3:17). The Kohathites became one of the major clans of the Levites (Numbers 3:27). They were responsible for the care of the most holy things of the tabernacle (Numbers 3:29; 4.4,15). The Kohathites were given towns to live in among the tribes of Ephraim, Dan and Manasseh (Joshua 21:5). Notable descendants of Kohath included Moses, Aaron, and the priestly line (Exodus 6:18), as well as the musician Heman (1 Chronicles 6:33). The Kohathites remained faithful Levites throughout Israel's history (1 Chronicles 9:32; 2 Chronicles 20:19; 29.12; 34.12).

name: Merari
title: The third son of Levi and founder of the Merarites.
bio: Merari was the third son of Levi and the founder of the Merarite clan, one of the three main divisions of the Levites (Genesis 46:11; Exodus 6:16). The Merarites were responsible for the transportation and maintenance of the tabernacle's framework, pillars, bases, and related equipment during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness (Numbers 3:36; 4.29,33,42,45). They were also given specific duties in the tabernacle service (Numbers 7:8; 10.17). In the time of David, the Merarites were assigned various roles in the temple service, including gatekeepers, singers, and assistants to the priests (1 Chronicles 6:44; 9.14; 15.6,17; 23.6,21; 24.26,27; 26.10,19). The Merarites were allotted cities in the territories of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun (Joshua 21:7; 1 Chronicles 6:63). Members of the Merarite clan, such as Asaiah and Shemaiah, were involved in the reforms and restoration of temple worship during the reigns of Hezekiah and Josiah (2 Chronicles 29:12; 34.12).

name: Hamul
title: Son of Perez, grandson of Judah.
bio: Hamul was a son of Perez and a grandson of Judah, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles.

name: Hezron
title: Son of Perez, grandson of Judah, ancestor of David.
bio:
Hezron was the son of Perez and the grandson of Judah, as recorded in Genesis 46:12, Numbers 26:21, and 1 Chronicles 2:5. He was born in Canaan and was one of the 70 members of Jacob's household who migrated to Egypt during the time of Joseph. Hezron's descendants formed a clan within the tribe of Judah, known as the Hezronites (Numbers 26:6). 

Hezron is mentioned in the genealogy of King David in Ruth 4:18 and 1 Chronicles 2:9. He is also listed in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in Matthew 1:3 and Luke 3:33, emphasizing his importance in the lineage of the Messiah. 

According to 1 Chronicles 2:18, Hezron had several children, including Jerahmeel, Ram (the ancestor of King David), and Caleb. He married the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead, in his old age and had a son named Segub, who became the father of Jair. 

As a descendant of Judah and an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ, Hezron played a significant role in the history of Israel and the fulfillment of God's promises to His people.

name: Jashub
title: Son of Issachar, grandson of Jacob
bio: Jashub, also known as Yob, was a son of Issachar and a grandson of Jacob.

name: Puah
title: Son of Issachar, grandson of Jacob
bio: Puah, also known as Puvah, was a son of Issachar and grandson of Jacob, and his descendants were called the Punites.

name: Shimron
title: Son of Issachar and progenitor of the Shimronites.
bio: Shimron was a son of Issachar and the progenitor of the Shimronite clan within the tribe of Issachar.

name: Tola
title: Son of Issachar, ancestor of the Tolaites
bio: Tola was one of the sons of Issachar, mentioned in Genesis 46:13, Numbers 26:23, and 1 Chronicles 7:1. He was born to Issachar during the family's time in Canaan and went down to Egypt with Jacob's household. Tola became the ancestor of the Tolaite clan within the tribe of Issachar. In the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai, the Tolaite clan numbered 22,600 men (Numbers 26:23). Tola's descendants were among the Israelites who received an inheritance in the Promised Land. The mention of Tola in the genealogies highlights the growth and development of the tribe of Issachar from the time of the patriarchs to the settlement in Canaan.

name: Elon
title: A son of Zebulun and founder of the Elonites.
bio: Elon was a son of Zebulun and the founder of the Elonite clan within the tribe of Zebulun.

name: Jahleel
title: Son of Zebulun, grandson of Jacob, and a clan leader.
bio: Jahleel, son of Zebulun, was a grandson of Jacob and a clan leader.
meaning: wait for G-d [El]; [poss.] may G-d [El] show himself friendly

name: Sered
title: Son of Zebulun, ancestor of the Seredites
bio: Sered was a son of Zebulun and the ancestor of the Seredite clan.

name: Areli
title: Son of Gad, grandson of Jacob
bio: Areli, a son of Gad, is mentioned in the genealogy of Jacob and the census of the Israelites in the wilderness.

name: Arod
title: Son of Gad and founder of the Arodite clan
bio: Arod, son of Gad, was the founder of the Arodite clan (Genesis 46:16).

name: Eri
title: Son of Gad; head of the Erite clan.
bio: Eri was a son of Gad and the head of the Erite clan.

name: Ezbon
title: Son of Gad; head of the Oznite clan.
bio: Ezbon, also known as Ozni, was a son of Gad and the head of the Oznite clan.

name: Haggi
title: Son of Gad, grandson of Jacob.
bio: Haggi was a son of Gad and a grandson of Jacob, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.
meaning: festal; born on the feast day

name: Shuni
title: Son of Gad, ancestor of the Shunite clan.
bio: Shuni was a son of Gad and the ancestor of the Shunite clan within the tribe of Gad.

name: Ziphion
title: Son of Gad, progenitor of the Zephonites
bio: Ziphion (or Zephon), a son of Gad, was the ancestor of the Zephonite clan.

name: Beriah
title: Son of Asher and head of a clan
bio: Beriah was a son of Asher, one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Gen. 46:17). He was born to Asher in Canaan before the family migrated to Egypt. Beriah became the head of a clan within the tribe of Asher (Num. 26:44-45). His descendants, known as the Beriites, were among the clans that formed the tribe of Asher during the time of Moses and the conquest of Canaan (1Ch. 7:30-31). The inclusion of Beriah and his clan in the genealogies and census records of Israel demonstrates the importance of family lineage and tribal organization in Israelite society.

name: Heber
title: Son of Beriah, grandson of Asher.
bio: Heber was a son of Beriah and a grandson of Asher, one of the twelve sons of Israel (or 'Jacob') (Israel). He is mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Asher in Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles. In Numbers, the descendants of Heber are referred to as the Heberite clan. Heber's sister was Jael, and his brother was Malchiel. No further information is provided about Heber in the Bible. (Genesis 46:17; Numbers 26:45; 1 Chronicles 7:31).

name: Ishvah
title: Son of Asher, grandson of Jacob.
bio: Ishvah was a son of Asher and grandson of Jacob.

name: Ishvi
title: Son of Asher, grandson of Jacob.
bio: Ishvi (or Isui) was a son of Asher and grandson of Jacob.

name: Malchiel
title: Son of Beriah, grandson of Asher.
bio: Malchiel, son of Beriah and grandson of Asher, was the ancestor of the Malchielites.

name: Serah
title: Daughter of Asher, sister of Asher's sons
bio: Serah was the daughter of Asher and the sister of Asher's sons, as mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Asher.
meaning: one who explains, opens, extends; abundance

name: Ahiram
title: Son of Benjamin, founder of the Ahiramite clan
bio: Ahiram, also known as Aharah or Ehi, was a son of Benjamin and the founder of the Ahiramite clan.

name: Ard
title: Son of Benjamin, brother of Bela
bio: Ard, a son of Benjamin, is listed among the descendants of Jacob who went to Egypt during the famine.

name: Ashbel
title: Son of Benjamin, founder of the Ashbelite clan
bio: Ashbel was a son of Benjamin and the founder of the Ashbelite clan (Genesis 46:21).
meaning: poss. a form of] man of Baal; having a long upper lip

name: Becher
title: Son of Benjamin, listed among those who entered Egypt.
bio: Becher was a son of Benjamin and is listed among the family members who entered Egypt with Jacob.

name: Bela
title: Son of Benjamin, head of the Belaite clan
bio: Bela is mentioned in several passages (Genesis 46:21; Numbers 26:38; 1 Chronicles 7:6) as one of the sons of Benjamin, the youngest son of Israel (or 'Jacob'). He is consistently listed as the first among Benjamin's sons, suggesting his prominence within the family. In the census of the Israelites in the wilderness (Numbers 26), Bela is named as the head of the Belaite clan, one of the clans within the tribe of Benjamin. The descendants of Bela are also mentioned in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles, highlighting the continuity of his lineage. The repeated mention of Bela in these various contexts emphasizes his importance as a progenitor of the Benjamite tribe and the role of his clan in the history of Israel.

name: Gera
title: Descendant of Benjamin; ancestor of Ehud, a judge of Israel.
bio: Gera was a descendant of Benjamin and an ancestor of Ehud, a left-handed judge who delivered Israel from Moabite oppression.

name: Huppim
title: A descendant of Benjamin.
bio: Huppim, also known as Hupham or Huram, was a descendant of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles.

name: Muppim
title: A son of Benjamin.
bio: Muppim, also known as Shephupham, Shephuphan, or Shuphamite, was a son of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles.

name: Naaman
title: A son of Benjamin.
bio: Naaman, also known as Nohah, was one of the sons of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

name: Rosh
title: Son of Benjamin, grandson of Jacob
bio: Rosh (or Rapha) was a son of Benjamin and grandson of Jacob, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

name: Hushim
title: Son of Dan, ancestor of the Shuhamites.
bio: Hushim, also known as Shuham, was the son of Dan and the ancestor of the Shuhamite clan within the tribe of Dan.

name: Guni
title: Son of Naphtali, grandson of Jacob.
bio: Guni was a son of Naphtali and a grandson of Jacob, as listed in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.

name: Jahzeel
title: Son of Naphtali, grandson of Jacob, and a clan leader.
bio: Jahzeel (or Jahziel), son of Naphtali, was a grandson of Jacob and a clan leader.

name: Jezer
title: Son of Naphtali, founder of the Jezerite clan
bio: Jezer, a son of Naphtali, was the ancestor of the Jezerite clan.

name: Shillem
title: Son of Naphtali, ancestor of the Shillemites
bio: Shillem (or Shallum), a son of Naphtali and ancestor of the Shillemite clan.

name: Machir
title: Son of Manasseh; father (ie re-founder) of Gilead
bio: Machir was the son of Manasseh and the father  (ie re-founder) of Gilead, making him a significant ancestor of the tribe of Manasseh (Genesis 50:23; Numbers 26:29; 1 Chronicles 7:14). He is mentioned numerous times throughout the Old Testament, often in relation to the settlement and inheritance of the tribe of Manasseh. Machir's descendants, known as the Machirites, formed a substantial portion of the tribe (Numbers 26:29; Joshua 17:1). They were known for their military prowess and were praised in the Song of Deborah (Judges 5:14). The Machirites, along with the Reubenites and Gadites, conquered and settled in the land of Gilead, east of the Jordan River (Numbers 32:39; Deuteronomy 3:15; Joshua 13:31). Machir's daughters, Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah, appealed to Moses for the right to inherit their father's property in the absence of male heirs, setting a precedent for inheritance laws (Numbers 27:1; 36.1; Joshua 17:3). Machir's descendants continued to play a role in the tribe of Manasseh, with some even marrying into the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:21).

name: Pharaoh
title: Egyptian Pharaoh during Moses' birth and early life
bio:
This Pharaoh was the Egyptian ruler during the time of Moses' birth and early life (Exodus 1-2). Fearing the growing Hebrew population, Pharaoh enslaved the Israelites and subjected them to hard labor. He ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill any male infants born to the Israelites, but they disobeyed, claiming that Hebrew women gave birth too quickly. Pharaoh then commanded that all Hebrew male infants be thrown into the Nile River. 

During this time, Moses was born and hidden by his mother for three months. When she could no longer hide him, she placed him in a basket among the reeds of the Nile. Pharaoh's daughter discovered the baby and decided to adopt him, unknowingly hiring Moses' mother as his nurse. Moses grew up in Pharaoh's court, but he later fled Egypt after killing an Egyptian who was mistreating a Hebrew (Exodus 2:11; Acts 7:21; Hebrews 11:24). 

The Bible does not provide the specific name or historical identity of this Pharaoh, as the term "Pharaoh" was used as a title for Egyptian kings. Some scholars suggest that this Pharaoh may have been from the 18th or 19th Dynasty of the New Kingdom period, possibly Thutmose I, Thutmose II, or Amenhotep I, based on the historical and archaeological evidence of the Israelites' presence in Egypt.

name: Puah
title: Hebrew midwife in Egypt
bio: Puah, one of the two Hebrew midwives, along with Shiphrah, who defied Pharaoh's order to kill male Hebrew babies.

name: Shiphrah
title: Hebrew midwife who feared God and disobeyed Pharaoh.
bio: Shiphrah, along with Puah, was a Hebrew midwife who feared God and disobeyed Pharaoh's command to kill male babies.

name: Daughter of Pharaoh
title: Daughter of Pharaoh - Rescued and adopted Moses

pharaoh-3.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio: Pharaoh's daughter rescued the infant Moses from the Nile and adopted him as her son.

name: Moses
title: Prophet who led Israel out of Egypt
bio:
Moses was born to Amram and Jochebed, Levites in Egypt, at a time when Pharaoh had commanded that all Hebrew male infants be killed (Exodus 2:1). His mother hid him for three months, then placed him in a basket on the Nile where Pharaoh's daughter found and adopted him (Exodus 2:3). As an adult, Moses killed an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew and fled to Midian (Exodus 2:11). There he married Zipporah and worked as a shepherd for his father-in-law Jethro (Exodus 2:16). 

God appeared to Moses in a burning bush and called him to lead Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3-4). Moses, along with his brother Aaron, went to Pharaoh demanding that he let Israel go (Exodus 5:1). Through a series of ten plagues, God compelled Pharaoh to release the Israelites (Exodus 7-12). Moses led them out of Egypt, through the Red Sea, and to Mount Sinai (Exodus 13-19). There God gave Moses the law and instructions for the tabernacle (Exodus 20-31). 

While Moses was on the mountain, Israel made and worshiped a golden calf (Exodus 32). Moses interceded for the people and God relented from destroying them (Exodus 32-34). Moses oversaw the construction of the tabernacle (Exodus 35-40). He led Israel for forty years in the wilderness, mediating between them and God (Numbers, Deuteronomy). God prohibited Moses from entering Canaan because of his disobedience at Meribah (Numbers 20:1). Before his death, Moses viewed the promised land from Mount Nebo (Deuteronomy 34:1). He died at 120 years old and was buried by God (Deuteronomy 34:5). 

The New Testament refers to Moses as the giver of the law (John 1:17), a type of Christ (John 3:14), and the greatest prophet of the old covenant (Acts 3:22). 

He is named "Manasseh" in several manuscripts of Judges 18.30 to save shaming his name when his grandson set up an idol.

name: Jethro
title: Moses' father-in-law, priest of Midian
bio:
Jethro, also referred to as Reuel, was Moses' father-in-law and a priest of Midian. He is first mentioned in Exodus 2:18, where his daughters tell him about Moses defending them at a well. Later, in Exodus 3:1, Moses is described as tending Jethro's flock when he encounters the burning bush. 

After the Exodus, Jethro visits Moses in the wilderness, bringing along Moses' wife Zipporah and their two sons (Exodus 18:1). Jethro praises God for the Israelites' deliverance from Egypt (Exodus 18:9) and offers sacrifices to God (Exodus 18:12). 

Observing Moses' heavy workload in judging the people, Jethro advises him to appoint capable men to share the burden (Exodus 18:13). Moses follows this advice and bids farewell to Jethro, who returns to his own land (Exodus 18:24). In Numbers 10:29, Moses invites Hobab, identified as Reuel's son, to join the Israelites on their journey, suggesting a continued relationship between Moses and Jethro's family.

name: Zipporah
title: Wife of Moses, daughter of Jethro

jethro.note: Named in the same passage, but Scripture doesn't state this word for word.

bio: Zipporah, the daughter of Jethro, was Moses' wife and the mother of his two sons, Gershom and Eliezer.

name: Gershom
title: Son of Moses; father of Jonathan, a renegade priest.

zipporah.note: Named in the same passage, but Scripture doesn't state this word for word.

bio: Gershom was the firstborn son of Moses and Zipporah, born during Moses' exile in Midian (Exodus 2:22). His name, which means "a stranger there," reflects Moses' feelings of being a foreigner in a strange land. Later, when Moses returned to Egypt to lead the Israelites out of slavery, Gershom and his brother Eliezer were reunited with their father (Exodus 18:3). As a descendant of Levi, Gershom and his descendants were counted among the Levites and assigned duties in the tabernacle and temple service (1 Chronicles 23:15). However, one of Gershom's descendants, Jonathan, became involved in idolatrous worship. According to Judges 18:30, Jonathan and his sons served as priests for the tribe of Dan, who had set up a graven image and a shrine. This incident highlights the spiritual decline among some of the Levites and the Israelites during the period of the judges. Despite this unfaithful descendant, Gershom's lineage remained significant within the Levitical priesthood, as evidenced by the mention of his descendants in the genealogies of Chronicles.

name: Pharaoh
title: Egyptian Pharaoh during the Exodus
bio:
This Pharaoh was the Egyptian ruler during the time of the Exodus (Exodus 3-14). When Moses and Aaron approached Pharaoh, demanding that he let the Israelites go, Pharaoh refused and increased their labor. God then sent a series of ten plagues upon Egypt, each time giving Pharaoh the opportunity to release the Israelites. However, Pharaoh repeatedly hardened his heart and refused to let them go until the tenth and final plague, the death of the firstborn. 

After the death of his own firstborn son, Pharaoh finally relented and allowed the Israelites to leave Egypt. However, he soon changed his mind and pursued them with his army. God parted the Red Sea for the Israelites to cross on dry land, but when the Egyptian army attempted to follow, the sea closed in on them, drowning Pharaoh and his forces (Exodus 14:28; Psalm Exodus 136:15). 

This Pharaoh is depicted as a stubborn and proud ruler who refused to acknowledge the power and authority of the God of Israel. His story serves as a reminder of God's sovereignty and His ability to deliver His people from oppression (Romans 9:17). The Bible does not provide the specific name or historical identity of this Pharaoh, but some scholars suggest that he may have been Amenhotep II, Thutmose III, or Ramesses II, based on the historical and archaeological evidence.

name: Aaron
title: Moses' brother, first high priest of Israel
bio:
Aaron was the older brother of Moses and Miriam, from the tribe of Levi. God appointed Aaron to be Moses' spokesman when Moses was called to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. Aaron performed signs before Pharaoh, including turning his staff into a snake. He assisted Moses during the Exodus, including holding up Moses' arms during the battle against the Amalekites. 

God chose Aaron and his descendants to serve as priests for the Israelites. Aaron was consecrated as the first high priest and wore special priestly garments. He was responsible for offering sacrifices, burning incense, and performing other priestly duties in the tabernacle. Aaron also played a role in several significant events, such as the golden calf incident and the rebellion of Korah. 

Aaron married Elisheba, and they had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord. Aaron died at the age of 123 on Mount Hor, and his son Eleazar succeeded him as high priest. Despite his flaws, Aaron was a key figure in Israel's history and played a crucial role in establishing the priesthood.

name: Libni
title: Son of Gershon; grandson of Levi
bio: Libni, also known as Ladan, was a son of Gershon and a grandson of Levi (Exodus 6:17; Numbers 3:18; 1 Chronicles 6:17). He was the brother of Shimei (Exodus 6:17; Numbers 3:18; 1 Chronicles 6:17; 23.7). Libni's descendants, the Libnites, were one of the Levitical clans (Numbers 3:21; 26.58). During the time of David, the Libnites were counted among the Levites and given duties in the service of the tabernacle (1 Chronicles 23:7). The sons of Libni, Jehiel and Zetham, along with their relatives, were given charge of the treasuries of the house of the Lord (1 Chronicles 26:21).

name: Shimei
title: Son of Gershon and grandson of Levi.
bio: Shimei was the son of Gershon and the grandson of Levi (Num. 3:18; Ex. 6:17; 1Ch. 6:17). He was one of the three main divisions of the Levites, along with the descendants of Kohath and Merari. The Shimites, his descendants, formed a clan within the Levites (Num. 3:21) and were responsible for various duties in the tabernacle and temple service. In the time of David, the Shimites were among the Levites appointed to serve in the house of the Lord (1Ch. 23:7, 10). The clan of Shimei is also mentioned in the prophetic vision of Zechariah, where they are listed among the Levitical families that will mourn and seek cleansing from sin (Zec. 12:13).

name: Amram
title: Father of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
bio: Amram was a Levite, the son of Kohath and father of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam (Exodus 6:18; Numbers 26:58; 1 Chronicles 6:2; 23.12,13). He married his father's sister Jochebed (Exodus 6:20). Amram's family belonged to the Kohathite branch of Levites (Numbers 3:19; 1 Chronicles 6:18; 24.20; 26.23). As the father of Moses and Aaron, Amram played a significant role in the history of Israel, although little is recorded about his own life.

name: Hebron
title: Son of Kohath, grandson of Levi.
bio: Hebron was a son of Kohath and a grandson of Levi. He is mentioned in the genealogies of the Levites in Exodus, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles. Hebron's brothers were Amram, Izhar, and Uzziel (Exodus 6:18; Numbers 3:19; 1 Chronicles 6:2). His descendants were known as the Hebronites, who were assigned various duties in the service of the tabernacle and the temple (Numbers 3:27; 26.58; 1 Chronicles 26:23). Some of the notable Hebronites included Jeriah, the chief of the Hebronites during the time of David (1 Chronicles 23:19; 26.31), and Hashabiah, a leader during the time of David (1 Chronicles 15:9).

name: Izhar
title: Son of Kohath, grandson of Levi; father of Korah.
bio:
Izhar, also known as Amminadab, was a Levite, the son of Kohath and grandson of Levi (Exo. 6:18, 21; Num. 3:19; 1Ch. 6:2, 18, 38). He was the father of Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri (Exo. 6:21; 1Ch. 6:22). Izhar's descendants, the Izharites, were one of the clans of the Kohathites (Num. 3:27; 1Ch. 24:22; 26:23, 29). 

The Kohathites, including the Izharites, were responsible for carrying the sacred objects of the tabernacle during Israel's journey in the wilderness (Num. 4:15, 18-20). They were also assigned duties in the tabernacle and, later, in the temple (1Ch. 6:33-38; 23:12-20; 24:20-31). Some of the Izharites served as officials and judges during King David's reign (1Ch. 26:29-30). 

Izhar's most notable descendant was Korah, who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron (Num. 16:1). Despite Korah's rebellion, the Izharites continued to serve as Levites in Israel.

name: Uzziel
title: Son of Kohath, uncle of Moses and Aaron
bio: Uzziel was a Levite, the son of Kohath and grandson of Levi. He was the brother of Amram, making him the uncle of Moses and Aaron. Uzziel had three sons: Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri. His descendants, the Uzzielites, were one of the Levite clans responsible for the care and transportation of the tabernacle. Uzziel's son Elzaphan and his brother Mishael were called by Moses to carry away the bodies of Nadab and Abihu after they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord. The descendants of Uzziel were also counted in the census of the Levites and given specific duties in the service of the tabernacle.

name: Mahli
title: Son of Merari, grandson of Levi.
bio: Mahli was one of the sons of Merari and a grandson of Levi. He was an ancestor of the Levitical clan known as the Mahlites. Mahli's descendants were responsible for various duties in the tabernacle and later in the temple. They were counted in the census of the Levites during the time of Moses and were given specific responsibilities in the transportation and setup of the tabernacle

name: Mushi
title: A Levite, son of Merari, and head of a clan.
bio:
Mushi was a Levite who lived during the time of Moses and the Exodus. He was the son of Merari, one of the three sons of Levi, and the grandson of Levi himself (Exodus 6:19; Numbers 3:20; 1 Chronicles 6:19). Mushi's descendants formed a clan within the Levitical tribe known as the Mushites (Numbers 3:33). 

As a member of the Levitical tribe, Mushi and his descendants were responsible for assisting the priests in the tabernacle and later in the temple. In the wilderness, the Mushites were specifically assigned to carry the frames, crossbars, posts, and bases of the tabernacle whenever the Israelites moved camp (Numbers 3:36). 

The descendants of Mushi are mentioned in several genealogies in 1 Chronicles, which trace the lineage of the Levites. These passages highlight the importance of the Levitical clans in maintaining the religious life of ancient Israel (1 Chronicles 23:21). 

Mushi's role as the head of a Levitical clan emphasizes the hereditary nature of the Levitical priesthood and the importance of family lineage in determining one's responsibilities within the religious system of ancient Israel. The Mushites, along with the other Levitical clans, played a vital role in supporting the priests and ensuring the proper functioning of the tabernacle and temple worship.

name: Jochebed
title: Mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
bio: Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, married her nephew Amram and became the mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

name: Korah
title: Levite rebel leader; his descendants became temple servants
bio: Korah was a Levite who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness (Num.16). He was the son of Izhar, from the Kohathite clan (Exodus 6:21). Korah, along with Dathan, Abiram, and 250 well-known community leaders, accused Moses and Aaron of exalting themselves above the congregation (Numbers 16:1). When Korah's followers presented incense offerings, the Lord destroyed them with fire (Numbers 16:35). The earth opened and swallowed Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and their households (Numbers 16:31). Korah's sons, however, did not die (Numbers 26:11). The bronze censers of the rebels were made into a covering for the altar, as a reminder not to rebel against the Lord (Numbers 16:38). Korah's descendants became temple musicians (1 Chronicles 6:22; Psa.42-49; 84-88) and gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 9:19; 26.1,19). Some were mighty warriors who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:6), and others settled in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9:31). The Korahites also sang at the reign of Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 20:19) and were listed among the Levite clans (Numbers 26:58).

name: Nepheg
title: Son of Izhar, from the tribe of Levi.
bio: Nepheg was a son of Izhar and a member of the Levite clan of Kohath.

name: Zichri
title: Son of Izhar, a Levite
bio: Zichri was a son of Izhar and grandson of Kohath, of the tribe of Levi.

name: Elizaphan
title: A Levite leader from the Kohathite clan.
bio: Elizaphan was a Levite leader from the clan of Kohath (Numbers 3:30). He was the son of Uzziel, who was the brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron (Exodus 6:22). Elizaphan and his brother Mishael were instructed by Moses to carry the bodies of Nadab and Abihu, Aaron's sons who were killed for offering unauthorized fire before the Lord (Leviticus 10:4). During the time of King David, Elizaphan's descendants, Shemaiah and his sons, were among the Levites appointed to carry the ark of the covenant (1 Chronicles 15:8). Later, during the reign of King Hezekiah, a descendant of Elizaphan named Shimri is mentioned as one of the Levites who helped cleanse and consecrate the temple (2 Chronicles 29:13). The Bible portrays Elizaphan and his descendants as having significant roles in the tabernacle and temple service throughout Israel's history.

name: Mishael
title: A Levite who helped remove the bodies of Nadab and Abihu.
bio: Mishael, a Levite and cousin of Aaron, assisted in removing the bodies of Nadab and Abihu after they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord.

name: Sithri
title: Son of Uzziel, a Levite of the Kohathite clan.
bio: Sithri was a son of Uzziel, a Levite of the Kohathite clan, mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites.

name: Abihu
title: Son of Aaron

elisheba.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio:
Abihu was the second son of Aaron and Elisheba, and the brother of Nadab, Eleazar, and Ithamar (Exodus 6:23; Numbers 3:2). He was consecrated as a priest along with his brothers to serve at the tabernacle (Exodus 28:1). Abihu went up Mount Sinai with Moses, Aaron, Nadab and seventy elders of Israel to worship the Lord before He gave the tablets of the Testimony to Moses (Exodus 24:1). 

However, Abihu and his brother Nadab offered unauthorized fire before the Lord, and fire came out from the presence of the Lord and consumed them, and they died (Leviticus 10:1; Numbers 3:4). This occurred on the eighth day of the priests' consecration. Aaron and his surviving sons were not allowed to mourn their deaths (Leviticus 10:6). 

The sin of Abihu and Nadab was in offering "strange fire" which the Lord had not commanded (Leviticus 10:1). This may refer to offering incense that was not prepared according to God's instructions, or performing this in a wrong manner or at an inappropriate time. Their deaths served as a stern warning against improper worship. After this incident, God gave Aaron further regulations for priestly service and conduct (Leviticus 10:8). The genealogies record Aaron's descendants through his other sons Eleazar and Ithamar, since Nadab and Abihu had no children before their untimely deaths (Numbers 3:4; 1 Chronicles 24:1).

name: Amminadab
title: Father-in-law of Aaron, ancestor of David
bio:
Amminadab was a prominent figure in the genealogy of the Israelites. He was the father of Elisheba, who married Aaron, the first high priest of Israel. Amminadab's son Nahshon was a leader of the tribe of Judah during the wilderness wanderings. Nahshon was in charge of the Judahite division and made offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle. 

Amminadab is also mentioned in the genealogy of King David, being his great-great-grandfather. This makes Amminadab an ancestor of Jesus Christ as well, as seen in the genealogies recorded in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke. 

The consistency of Amminadab's mention in various genealogical records highlights his significance in the lineage of important biblical figures, from the time of Moses to the earthly life of Jesus.

name: Eleazar
title: Son of Aaron, high priest after his father

elisheba.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio: Eleazar, the son of Aaron, is prominently featured in the books of Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, and 1 Chronicles. He was the third son of Aaron and Elisheba (Exodus 6:23) and was consecrated as a priest along with his brothers (Exodus 28:1). After the deaths of his older brothers, Nadab and Abihu (Leviticus 10:1), Eleazar became the chief priest under his father (Numbers 3:32). He assisted Moses in the census (Numbers 26:1) and the allocation of lands to the tribes (Numbers 32:2; Joshua 14:1). Eleazar succeeded Aaron as high priest (Numbers 20:25; Deuteronomy 10:6) and served in that role during the conquest of Canaan (Joshua 21:1). He played a key role in the distribution of the Levitical cities (Joshua 21:1) and died during the time of Joshua (Joshua 24:33). His descendants continued to serve as priests (Judges 20:28; 1 Chronicles 6:3; Ezra 7:5).

name: Elisheba
title: Aaron's wife and Nahshon's daughter.
bio: Elisheba was the wife of Aaron and the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon.
meaning: G-d [El] is an oath; G-d [El] is my fill

name: Ithamar
title: Youngest son of Aaron; served as priest.

elisheba.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio:
Ithamar was the fourth and youngest son of Aaron, the first high priest of Israel (Exodus 6:23). He served as a priest alongside his brothers Nadab, Abihu, and Eleazar (Numbers 3:2). After the deaths of Nadab and Abihu for offering unauthorized fire before the Lord (Leviticus 10:1), Ithamar and Eleazar were warned not to mourn for them openly (Leviticus 10:6). 

Ithamar assisted his father Aaron and his brother Eleazar in their priestly duties (Exodus 28:1; Numbers 3:4). He was responsible for overseeing the Gershonites and Merarites, two of the Levite clans, in their tabernacle duties (Numbers 4:28). During the dedication of the tabernacle, Ithamar assisted Moses in receiving the offerings from the tribal leaders (Numbers 7:8). 

Ithamar's descendants continued to serve as priests (1 Chronicles 24:1). They were divided into divisions for their appointed duties, just as Aaron's other descendants were. One of Ithamar's notable descendants was Eli, who served as high priest and judge in Israel (1 Samuel 14:3; 1 Kings 2:27). 

In Ezra 8:2, a descendant of Ithamar named Daniel is mentioned among the priests who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile. This highlights the continuity of Ithamar's lineage in the priesthood.

name: Nadab
title: Son of Aaron, consumed by fire for offering incense.

elisheba.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio:
Nadab was the eldest son of Aaron, the first High Priest of Israel, and his wife Elisheba (Exodus 6:23). Along with his brothers Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, Nadab was consecrated as a priest to serve in the Tabernacle (Exodus 28:1). 

Nadab, along with his brother Abihu and seventy elders of Israel, accompanied Moses partway up Mount Sinai when the Lord made His covenant with the people (Exodus 24:1). There, they saw a manifestation of God's presence and ate and drank in His presence. 

However, Nadab and Abihu later committed a grave offense by offering unauthorized fire (incense) before the Lord, which He had not commanded them to do (Leviticus 10:1). As a result, fire came out from the presence of the Lord and consumed them, and they died before the Lord (Leviticus 10:2; Numbers 3:4). 

This tragic event served as a sobering reminder to the Israelites of the importance of following God's commands precisely, especially in matters related to worship and the priesthood. After their death, Eleazar and Ithamar took over their priestly duties under the direction of their father, Aaron (Numbers 3:4; 1 Chronicles 24:2). 

The story of Nadab and Abihu underscores the holiness of God and the seriousness with which He regards the proper worship and service of His people. It also highlights the importance of obedience and the consequences of disregarding God's clear instructions.

name: Assir
title: Son of Korah who is grandson of Kohath
bio: Assir was a son of Korah and great-grandson of Kohath, from the tribe of Levi (Exodus 6:24).

name: Ebiasaph
title: Levite descendant of Korah, ancestor of temple gatekeepers

korah.note: Exodus 6:24 says this directly. Other verses name Elkanah in between, so it's shown as a line of descent.

bio:
Ebiasaph, also known as Abiasaph or Asaph, is mentioned in several genealogies in the Old Testament. He was a descendant of Korah, the Levite who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness (Numbers 16). 

In the genealogies of the Levites in 1 Chronicles 6:23, Ebiasaph is listed as the son of Korah and the ancestor of the temple singers and musicians. This genealogy traces the lineage of the Levites from the time of Moses to the reign of King David. 

Ebiasaph is also mentioned in Exodus 6:24 as one of the sons of Korah, along with Assir and Elkanah. This passage is part of the genealogy of the Levites, specifically the descendants of Kohath, who were responsible for carrying the sacred objects of the tabernacle during the Israelites' wilderness wanderings. 

In 1 Chronicles 9:19, Ebiasaph is identified as an ancestor of the gatekeepers of the tabernacle. The gatekeepers were responsible for guarding the entrances to the sacred areas and ensuring that only authorized personnel could enter. 

Furthermore, in 1 Chronicles 26:1, Ebiasaph is mentioned as the ancestor of a division of gatekeepers during the time of King David. This passage describes the organization of the Levites and their duties in the temple service. 

The interchangeable use of the names Ebiasaph, Abiasaph, and Asaph in these passages suggests that they refer to the same individual. The variations in spelling may be due to differences in transliteration or scribal traditions. 

Ebiasaph's inclusion in these genealogies highlights the importance of the Levitical lineage and their roles in the tabernacle and temple service. As a descendant of Korah, Ebiasaph's family line was redeemed from the rebellion and given the privilege of serving in the house of the Lord.

name: Elkanah
title: A Levite descendant of Korah.
bio: Elkanah was a Levite descendant of Korah, the son of Izhar.

name: Phinehas
title: Aaron's grandson; zealous priest who opposed idolatry

daughter-of-putiel-exo-6-25.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio:
Phinehas was the son of Eleazar and the grandson of Aaron, the first high priest of Israel (Exodus 6:25). He is most remembered for his zealous act of killing an Israelite man and a Midianite woman who were engaging in sexual immorality and idolatry, thus turning away God's wrath from the people (Numbers 25:7). As a result, God granted Phinehas and his descendants a covenant of perpetual priesthood (Numbers 25:12; Psalm Numbers 106:30). 

Phinehas also played important roles in other events. He was sent along with other leaders to confront the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh regarding an altar they had built, which was seen as a potential act of rebellion against God (Joshua 22:13). He served as a priest during the time of the judges and was consulted before the Israelites went to battle against the tribe of Benjamin (Judges 20:28). 

Phinehas was succeeded by his son Abishua in the line of high priests (1 Chronicles 6:4). He was remembered as a faithful priest who had charge of the gatekeepers in the tabernacle (1 Chronicles 9:20) and was part of Ezra's lineage (Ezra 7:5).

name: Putiel
title: Father-in-law of Eleazar, son of Aaron
bio: Putiel was the father-in-law of Eleazar, son of Aaron.

name: Daughter of Putiel
title: Daughter of Putiel - Wife of Eleazar the priest

putiel-1.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio: The daughter of Putiel was the wife of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest.

name: Miriam
title: Moses' sister, a prophetess who led women in worship.

jochebed.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio:
Miriam was the sister of Moses and Aaron, and a prominent figure in the Exodus narrative. She first appears in Exodus 15:20, where she is described as a prophetess who led the women of Israel in worship and dance after the crossing of the Red Sea. This event highlights her leadership role among the women and her musical abilities. 

However, Miriam's life was not without controversy. In Numbers 12:1, she and Aaron criticized Moses for marrying a Cushite woman and challenged his authority as God's chosen leader. As a result, God punished Miriam with leprosy, but she was healed after Moses interceded on her behalf. This incident serves as a warning against questioning God's appointed leaders. 

Miriam's death is recorded in Numbers 20:1, which takes place near the end of the Israelites' forty years of wandering in the wilderness. Her significance in Israel's history is further emphasized in Micah 6:4, where she is mentioned alongside Moses and Aaron as one of the leaders God sent to guide the people out of Egypt.
meaning: [variously] bitterness; plump one; wished-for child; one who loves or is loved

name: Joshua
title: Moses' assistant who led Israel into Canaan

ephraim.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio:
Joshua, the son of Nun, was a prominent figure in the Old Testament who served as Moses' assistant and later succeeded him as the leader of the Israelites. He was from the tribe of Ephraim (Numbers 13:8) and was originally named Hoshea, but Moses changed his name to Joshua (Numbers 13:16). Joshua was one of the twelve spies sent to explore the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:8), and he and Caleb were the only ones who brought back a positive report and encouraged the people to trust God (Numbers 14:6). As a result, Joshua and Caleb were the only adults from their generation permitted to enter the Promised Land (Numbers 14:30). 

Before Moses' death, God appointed Joshua to succeed him as the leader of Israel (Numbers 27:18; Deuteronomy 31:7). After Moses' death, Joshua led the Israelites across the Jordan River and into the land of Canaan (Joshua 1-4). He oversaw the conquest of Jericho (Joshua 6), Ai (Joshua 8), and numerous other cities and territories (Joshua 10-12). Joshua also led the Israelites in renewing their covenant with God (Joshua 8:30). 

Under Joshua's leadership, the land of Canaan was divided among the tribes of Israel as their inheritance (Joshua 13-21). In his old age, Joshua gave a farewell address to the Israelites, encouraging them to remain faithful to God (Joshua 23-24). He died at the age of 110 and was buried in his inheritance at Timnath-serah (Joshua 24:29; Judges 2:8). 

Joshua is remembered as a courageous leader, a faithful servant of God, and a key figure in Israel's history who led the people into the Promised Land and helped establish them as a nation.

name: Hur
title: A companion of Moses and grandfather of Bezalel.
bio:
Hur was a significant figure in the early history of Israel, particularly during the Israelites' journey in the wilderness after their exodus from Egypt. He is mentioned several times in the books of Exodus and Chronicles. 

In Exodus 17:10, Hur is described as one of the two men who accompanied Moses to the top of a hill during the battle against the Amalekites. Along with Aaron, Hur supported Moses' arms, which were holding the staff of God. As long as Moses' hands were raised, Israel prevailed in the battle. Hur's presence and assistance were crucial in securing the victory. 

Later, in Exodus 24:14, Moses appointed Hur, along with Aaron, to oversee the people while he went up to Mount Sinai to receive the tablets of the law from God. This indicates that Hur was a trusted and respected leader among the Israelites. 

Hur is also mentioned in the context of the construction of the tabernacle. In Exodus 31:2 and Exodus 35:30, God appointed Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, as the chief artisan responsible for crafting the tabernacle and its furnishings. This connection suggests that Hur's family was skilled in craftsmanship and held a prominent position within the tribe of Judah.

name: Eliezer
title: Son of Moses and Zipporah.

zipporah.note: Named in the same passage, but Scripture doesn't state this word for word.

bio: Eliezer was the second son of Moses and Zipporah (Exodus 18:4). His name, which means "my God is help," was given by Moses because God had delivered him from Pharaoh's sword (Exodus 18:4). Eliezer and his brother Gershom were born during Moses' exile in Midian. In the genealogies of the Levites, Eliezer is listed as a son of Moses (1 Chronicles 23:15). He had a son named Rehabiah, who had many descendants (1 Chronicles 23:17; 26.25). The Bible does not provide any further details about Eliezer's life or role.

name: Bezalel
title: Skilled craftsman who built the tabernacle
bio: Bezalel, the son of Uri and grandson of Hur from the tribe of Judah, was a skilled craftsman chosen by God to oversee the construction of the tabernacle and its furnishings (Exo. 31:2; 35:30; 1Ch. 2:20). God filled Bezalel with His Spirit, giving him wisdom, understanding, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship, including working with gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood (Exo. 31:3-5). Bezalel, along with Oholiab from the tribe of Dan, led the skilled workers in creating the tabernacle, the ark of the covenant, the altar, and all the other sacred items according to the divine instructions given to Moses (Exo. 36:1-2; 37:1; 38:22). Bezalel's exceptional skills and divine empowerment underscore the importance of the tabernacle as a place where God's presence would dwell among His people. The tabernacle and its furnishings, crafted by Bezalel, were later brought to Jerusalem by King Solomon (2Ch. 1:5).

name: Uri
title: Father of Bezalel, the skilled craftsman
bio: Uri, the son of Hur from the tribe of Judah, is mentioned in Exodus 31:2:30, and Exodus 38:22, as well as 1 Chronicles 2:20, as the father of Bezalel. Bezalel was the skilled craftsman chosen by God and filled with the Spirit of God to construct the tabernacle and its furnishings, including the ark of the covenant. Uri's grandson, Bezalel, is also mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles 2:20, emphasizing the family's important role in the construction of the tabernacle. Apart from being the father of Bezalel, no other details are provided about Uri's life or his own role in the community.

name: Ahisamach
title: Father of Oholiab, a skilled artisan for the tabernacle
bio: Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, was the father of Oholiab, a skilled artisan who helped construct the tabernacle.

name: Oholiab
title: Skilled craftsman for the tabernacle
bio: Oholiab was a skilled craftsman from the tribe of Dan who was appointed by God to work alongside Bezalel in the construction of the tabernacle (Exodus 31:6). He was filled with the Spirit of God and given wisdom, understanding, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship (Exodus 35:34). Oholiab and Bezalel were responsible for overseeing the work of the tabernacle and creating the sacred furnishings and garments according to the divine instructions given to Moses (Exodus 36:1). Their skillful work was essential in establishing a place of worship for the Israelites during their journey in the wilderness.

name: Nun
title: Father of Joshua

elishama-1.note: Named in the same passage, but Scripture doesn't state this word for word.

bio: Nun was an Israelite from the tribe of Ephraim, best known as the father of Joshua (Exodus 33:11). His son Joshua was Moses' assistant from his youth (Numbers 11:28) and was chosen by God to succeed Moses as the leader of Israel (Numbers 27:18; Deuteronomy 31:23). Nun's name is often mentioned in connection with Joshua, emphasizing the importance of family lineage and the faithfulness passed down through generations. Joshua is referred to as "Joshua the son of Nun" throughout the Bible (e.g., Numbers 14:6; Joshua 1:1). As the father of a prominent leader, Nun's legacy was remembered long after his lifetime (1 Kings 16:34; Nehemiah 8:17).

name: Dibri
title: Father of Shelomith, whose son blasphemed God's name
bio: Dibri, of the tribe of Dan, was the father of Shelomith, whose son blasphemed the name of God and was stoned to death.

name: Shelomith
title: Mother of a blasphemer
bio: Shelomith, the mother of a man who blasphemed God's name.

name: Elizur
title: A leader from the tribe of Reuben.
bio: Elizur, the son of Shedeur, was a prominent leader from the tribe of Reuben during the Israelites' wilderness journey after the Exodus from Egypt. He was appointed as the leader of the Reubenites and was responsible for organizing and leading the tribe in various aspects of the journey (Numbers 1:5). Elizur's duties included assisting in the census of the Israelites (Numbers 1:5), overseeing the encampment of the Reubenites on the south side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2:10), presenting the tribe's offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:30), and leading the Reubenites in the order of march (Numbers 10:18). As a tribal leader, Elizur played a significant role in the administrative and military organization of the Israelites during their time in the wilderness. The Bible does not provide any further details about Elizur's life or leadership beyond these specific responsibilities.

name: Shedeur
title: Father of Elizur, a leader of Reuben
bio:
Shedeur was the father of Elizur, a prominent leader from the tribe of Reuben. Elizur was chosen as the leader of the Reubenites in the census and organization of Israel in the wilderness (Numbers 1:5). He was in charge of the camp of Reuben, which was located on the south side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2:10). 

Elizur represented Reuben when the leaders brought offerings for the dedication of the altar. He brought his offering on the fourth day (Numbers 7:30). When the Israelites set out from Mount Sinai, Elizur led the tribe of Reuben, along with the Simeonites and the Gadites, as the second group in the order of march (Numbers 10:18). Shedeur is mentioned only in reference to his son Elizur and is not recorded as having any other role or significance himself.
meaning: Shaddai is light or Shaddai is fire

name: Shelumiel
title: Leader of the tribe of Simeon
bio:
Shelumiel was the son of Zurishaddai and the leader of the tribe of Simeon during the Israelites' wilderness wanderings. In the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai, Shelumiel was the one who stood with Moses and Aaron to number the Simeonites (Numbers 1:6). When the Israelites camped in the wilderness, Shelumiel and the Simeonites were positioned on the south side of the tabernacle, alongside the tribes of Reuben and Gad (Numbers 2:12). 

Shelumiel also had a prominent role in the dedication of the altar. On the fifth day of the dedication, he brought his offering on behalf of the tribe of Simeon, which included various silver and gold utensils and sacrificial animals (Numbers 7:36). When the Israelites set out from Mount Sinai, Shelumiel led the tribe of Simeon in the second division of the marching order, following the tabernacle (Numbers 10:19).

name: Zurishaddai
title: Father of Shelumiel, leader of Simeon
bio: Zurishaddai Zurishaddai was an Israelite of the tribe of Simeon. He was the father of Shelumiel, who was chosen as the leader of the tribe of Simeon during the census and organization of Israel in the wilderness (Numbers 1:6). Shelumiel presented the offering for the tribe of Simeon at the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:36) and led the tribe in the order of march through the wilderness (Numbers 10:19).

name: Nethanel
title: Leader of Issachar
bio: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Israelite tribe of Issachar during the wilderness wanderings under Moses (Numbers 1:8). He was appointed to help take the census (Numbers 1:8) and made offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:18). Nethanel and the men of Issachar marched under their tribal standard as part of the camp of Judah, on the east side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2:5). His name means "given of God."

name: Zuar
title: Father of Nethanel, leader of Issachar
bio: Zuar Zuar was an Israelite man of the tribe of Issachar. He was the father of Nethanel, who was chosen as the leader of the tribe of Issachar during the census and organization of Israel in the wilderness (Numbers 1:8). Nethanel presented the offering for the tribe of Issachar at the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:18). He also led the tribe of Issachar in the order of march through the wilderness (Numbers 10:15).

name: Eliab
title: Son of Helon, leader of the tribe of Zebulun
bio: Eliab, the son of Helon, is mentioned in Numbers 1:9; and Numbers 10:16 as the leader of the tribe of Zebulun during the Israelites' wilderness journey. He was appointed as the representative of his tribe during the census conducted by Moses and Aaron (Numbers 1:9). Eliab's tribe, along with the tribes of Judah and Issachar, camped on the east side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2:7). As the leader, Eliab presented the offering of the tribe of Zebulun during the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:24). He also led his tribe in the order of march when the Israelites set out from Mount Sinai (Numbers 10:16).

name: Helon
title: Father of Eliab, a leader from the tribe of Zebulun.
bio: Helon was an Israelite from the tribe of Zebulun who lived during the time of Moses. He was the father of Eliab, a prominent leader within the tribe (Numbers 1:9). Eliab was chosen as the leader of the Zebulunites during the census and organization of the Israelite camp in the wilderness (Numbers 2:7). He also represented his tribe when the leaders brought offerings for the dedication of the tabernacle altar (Numbers 7:24). Additionally, Eliab led the Zebulunites in the order of march when the Israelites set out from Mount Sinai (Numbers 10:16). Helon's mention in connection with his son Eliab suggests that he was a respected member of the tribe of Zebulun. (Numbers 1:9; 2.7; 7.24,29; 10.16).

name: Ammihud
title: Father of Elishama, leader of Ephraim

ephraim.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio: Ammihud was an Ephraimite, the father of Elishama, who was a prominent leader during the Israelites' wilderness journey. Elishama, the son of Ammihud, was the leader of the people of Ephraim and one of the tribal chiefs who assisted Moses in the census of the Israelites. He was also in charge of the camp of Ephraim, which included the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin. Additionally, Elishama presented the offering of the tribe of Ephraim during the dedication of the tabernacle. Ammihud is also mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Ephraim in the book of Chronicles.

name: Elishama
title: A leader from the tribe of Ephraim.
bio: Elishama was a leader from the tribe of Ephraim during the Israelites' wilderness journey after the Exodus from Egypt. He was the son of Ammihud (Numbers 1:10) and grandfather of Joshua (1 Chronicles 7:26). Elishama was appointed as the leader of the Ephraimites and was responsible for organizing and leading the tribe in the census, encampment, and offerings (Numbers 1:10; 2.18; 7.48,53; 10.22). As a tribal leader, he played a significant role in the administrative and military organization of the Israelites during their time in the wilderness. The Bible does not provide any further details about Elishama's life or leadership.

name: Gamaliel
title: Leader of the tribe of Manasseh during the Exodus.
bio: Gamaliel, the son of Pedahzur, was the leader of the tribe of Manasseh during the Israelites' journey from Egypt to the Promised Land. He is mentioned several times in the book of Numbers. In Numbers 1:10, Gamaliel is listed as the leader of Manasseh in the census taken at the beginning of the second year after the Exodus. The tribe of Manasseh, under Gamaliel's leadership, was counted as part of the larger Israelite community (Numbers 1:34). In the arrangement of the Israelite camp, Gamaliel and the tribe of Manasseh were positioned on the west side of the tabernacle, along with the tribes of Ephraim and Benjamin (Numbers 2:20). Gamaliel also had a role in the offerings presented at the dedication of the tabernacle. He brought his offering on the eighth day, which included various animals and vessels for the tabernacle service (Numbers 7:54). When the Israelites set out from Mount Sinai, Gamaliel and the tribe of Manasseh marched under their standard, as directed by God (Numbers 10:23). These references to Gamaliel highlight his leadership role and the importance of the tribe of Manasseh in the organization and journey of the Israelites through the wilderness.

name: Pedahzur
title: Father of Gamaliel, leader from Manasseh
bio: Pedahzur was the father of Gamaliel, who was the leader of the tribe of Manasseh during Israel's wilderness wanderings. In the census taken in the wilderness of Sinai, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was counted as the leader of Manasseh (Numbers 1:10). When the Israelites made offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle, Gamaliel brought his tribe's offering on the eighth day (Numbers 7:54). Gamaliel also led the tribe of Manasseh when the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai (Numbers 10:23). Pedahzur is only mentioned in reference to his son's leadership role.

name: Abidan
title: Leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Exodus
bio: Abidan, the son of Gideoni, was the leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness after the Exodus from Egypt. He is mentioned several times in the book of Numbers. Abidan was one of the leaders who assisted Moses in taking a census of the Israelite population (Numbers 1:11). He also led the Benjamite tribe when the Israelites camped and marched in the wilderness (Numbers 2:22). Additionally, Abidan presented the offering of the tribe of Benjamin during the dedication of the altar in the tabernacle (Numbers 7:60). Beyond these specific roles, no other details about Abidan's life or leadership are provided in the Bible.

name: Gideoni
title: Leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Exodus.
bio: He is first introduced in Numbers 1:11 during the census of the Israelite men of military age, where he is listed as the representative of Benjamin. In Numbers 2:22, Gideoni is described as the leader of the Benjamite camp, which was positioned on the west side of the tabernacle, along with the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh. During the offering of the dedicatory gifts for the altar, Gideoni presented the offering for the tribe of Benjamin on the ninth day (Numbers 7:60). In Numbers 10:24, Gideoni is mentioned again as the leader of the Benjamite division during the Israelites' march through the wilderness. His presence as a tribal leader throughout the book of Numbers highlights the importance of organization and leadership during the Israelites' journey to the Promised Land.

name: Ahiezer
title: Leader from the tribe of Dan during the Exodus
bio:
Ahiezer, the son of Ammishaddai, was a prominent leader from the tribe of Dan during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness. He was appointed by God as the head of his tribe and played a significant role in the census and organization of the Israelite camp. (Numbers 1:12; 2.25) 

Ahiezer's tribe was positioned on the north side of the tabernacle, along with the tribes of Asher and Naphtali. (Numbers 2:25) He presented his tribe's offering at the dedication of the tabernacle, which included a silver plate, a silver basin, and various animals for sacrifice. (Numbers 7:66) 

As a tribal leader, Ahiezer was responsible for leading the Danites in their journey and ensuring their obedience to God's commands. (Numbers 10:25)

name: Ammishaddai
title: Father of Ahiezer, leader of Dan
bio: Ammishaddai was the father of Ahiezer, a prominent leader from the tribe of Dan during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness. Ahiezer, the son of Ammishaddai, was appointed as the leader of the Danites and was responsible for overseeing the census of his tribe. He also led the tribe of Dan when the Israelites were encamped and during their journey. Additionally, Ahiezer presented the offering of the tribe of Dan at the dedication of the tabernacle.

name: Ochran
title: Father of Pagiel
bio: Ochran was an Israelite from the tribe of Asher. He was the father of Pagiel, who was chosen as the leader of the tribe during the Exodus (Numbers 1:13). Pagiel represented Asher in the census (Numbers 1:13), in the arrangement of the tribal camps (Numbers 2:27), and in the offerings presented at the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:72). He also led the tribe in the order of march (Numbers 10:26). Ochran's name is mentioned in connection with his son's leadership role, highlighting the importance of family lineage in the tribal structure of Israel.

name: Pagiel
title: Leader of the tribe of Asher
bio: Pagiel, son of Ochran, was the leader of the tribe of Asher during the Israelites' wilderness wanderings (Numbers 1:13). He is mentioned several times in the book of Numbers as one of the leaders who assisted Moses in the census and organization of the Israelite camp (Numbers 1:13). In the census, Pagiel was responsible for counting the men of military age in his tribe (Numbers 1:41). He also brought an offering on behalf of his tribe during the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:72). As the leader of Asher, Pagiel would have been responsible for overseeing the affairs of his tribe, settling disputes, and representing their interests before Moses and the other tribal leaders. His presence in the various lists and events in Numbers highlights the importance of the tribal structure and leadership in the organization and governance of the Israelite community during their journey through the wilderness.

name: Deuel
title: Father of Eliasaph, leader of the tribe of Gad
bio:
Deuel, also known as Reuel, is mentioned in the book of Numbers as the father of Eliasaph, who was the leader of the tribe of Gad during Israel's wilderness journey. In Numbers 1:14, Eliasaph is identified as the son of Deuel when Moses and Aaron take a census of the Israelites. 

Later, in Numbers 2:14, Eliasaph is again mentioned as the leader of the tribe of Gad, and his father's name is given as Reuel. This variation in names has led some scholars to conclude that Deuel and Reuel refer to the same person, with the names being used interchangeably. 

Eliasaph's leadership role is further highlighted in Numbers 7:42, where he presents the offering for the tribe of Gad during the dedication of the tabernacle. In Numbers 10:20, Eliasaph is once again mentioned as the leader of the Gadites when the Israelites set out from Mount Sinai. 

The mention of Deuel/Reuel in these passages serves to identify Eliasaph and emphasize his role as a tribal leader during a significant period in Israel's history. As the father of Eliasaph, Deuel/Reuel would have been a respected figure within the tribe of Gad.

name: Eliasaph
title: Son of Deuel, leader of the tribe of Gad
bio: Eliasaph, the son of Deuel (or Reuel), is mentioned in Numbers 1:14; and Numbers 10:20 as the leader of the tribe of Gad during the Israelites' wilderness journey. He was appointed as the representative of his tribe during the census conducted by Moses and Aaron (Numbers 1:14). Eliasaph's tribe, along with the tribes of Reuben and Simeon, camped on the south side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2:14). As the leader, Eliasaph presented the offering of the tribe of Gad during the dedication of the tabernacle (Numbers 7:42). He also led his tribe in the order of march when the Israelites set out from Mount Sinai (Numbers 10:20).

name: Ahira
title: Leader of the tribe of Naphtali during the Exodus
bio:
Ahira, the son of Enan, was a prominent leader of the tribe of Naphtali during the Israelites' exodus from Egypt and their subsequent journey through the wilderness. He was appointed by God as the head of his tribe and played a significant role in the organization and leadership of the Israelite community. (Numbers 1:15) 

In the arrangement of the Israelite camp, Ahira and the tribe of Naphtali were positioned on the north side of the tabernacle, along with the tribes of Dan and Asher. (Numbers 2:29). 

As a tribal leader, Ahira was responsible for presenting the offerings of the tribe of Naphtali during the dedication of the altar. He brought his offering on the twelfth day, which included various silver and gold utensils, as well as animals for sacrifices. (Numbers 7:78) 

When the Israelites set out from Mount Sinai, Ahira and the tribe of Naphtali were part of the rearguard, marching last among the tribal divisions. (Numbers 10:27) 

Throughout the wilderness journey, Ahira would have played a crucial role in leading his tribe, ensuring their obedience to God's commands, and representing their interests before Moses and the other tribal leaders. However, no further specific details about his life or leadership are recorded in the biblical text.
meaning: [my] brother is my friend or my brother is evil

name: Enan
title: Father of Ahira, a leader of the tribe of Naphtali.
bio: Enan is mentioned in the Bible as the father of Ahira, who was the leader of the tribe of Naphtali during the Israelites' wilderness journey after the Exodus from Egypt. Enan's name appears multiple times in the book of Numbers in connection with his son's leadership role. In the census of the Israelites taken in the wilderness of Sinai, Ahira son of Enan is listed as the leader of the tribe of Naphtali (Numbers 1:15). The tribe of Naphtali, under Ahira's leadership, was positioned on the north side of the tabernacle, along with the tribes of Dan and Asher (Numbers 2:29). During the dedication of the tabernacle, Ahira son of Enan brought the offering for the tribe of Naphtali on the twelfth day (Numbers 7:78). Later, when the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai, the tribe of Naphtali, led by Ahira, was assigned to march last, along with the tribes of Dan and Asher (Numbers 10:27). Although Enan himself is not mentioned in any other context, his repeated mention as the father of Ahira highlights the significance of family lineage in the leadership structure of the Israelite tribes during their wilderness journey.

name: Caleb
title: Faithful spy, given Hebron as inheritance
bio: Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, was one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan (Num. 13:6). Along with Joshua, Caleb stood firm in his faith and trust in God's promise, encouraging the Israelites to enter the land despite the other spies' negative report (Num. 13:30; 14:6-9). As a result, God commended Caleb for his faithfulness and promised that he would inherit the land he had explored (Num. 14:24, 30, 38; Deut. 1:36). After the conquest of Canaan, Caleb requested and received Hebron as his inheritance (Josh. 14:6-15; 15:13-19; 21:12; Judg. 1:12-15, 20). He drove out the Anakim giants from Hebron and offered his daughter Achsah in marriage to whoever conquered Kirjath Sepher (Josh. 15:14-17; Judg. 1:12-13). Caleb's descendants settled in the Negev region and in the cities of Hebron (1Sam. 30:14; 1Chr. 4:15; 6:56). His faith, courage, and obedience to God made him a prominent figure in Israel's history, and his story is remembered as an example of unwavering trust in God's promises (Num. 32:12; Judg. 3:9).

name: Jephunneh
title: The Kenizzite, father of Caleb the spy.
bio: Jephunneh, a Kenizzite, was the father of Caleb, a prominent figure in the Old Testament. Caleb was chosen as one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan. Along with Joshua, Caleb was one of the two spies who brought back a positive report and encouraged the Israelites to trust in God and take possession of the land. As a result, Caleb and Joshua were the only two adults from their generation permitted to enter Canaan. Jephunneh's Kenizzite background suggests that he may have been a descendant of the Kenizzites, a non-Israelite tribe that was later absorbed into the tribe of Judah. Caleb's inheritance in the Promised Land, including Hebron and its surrounding areas, is mentioned multiple times in connection with Jephunneh, emphasizing the faithfulness and obedience of this father-son duo.

name: Anak
title: Ancestor of giant people in Canaan

arba-jos-14-15.note: Read from the wording of the verse, which doesn't fix the relationship exactly.

bio:
Anak was the progenitor of the Anakim, a race of giants who lived in Canaan prior to the Israelite conquest. The Anakim were known for their great height and strength, which struck fear into the hearts of the Israelite spies who were sent to scout out the land. The spies reported that the descendants of Anak were among the inhabitants of Canaan, comparing them to the Nephilim, another race of giants. 

During the conquest of Canaan under Joshua's leadership, the Israelites fought against the Anakim and gradually drove them out of the land. Caleb, one of the faithful spies, was given Hebron as his inheritance, which was formerly known as Kiriath-arba and was associated with Anak. Caleb successfully expelled the descendants of Anak from Hebron. 

The Anakim were also mentioned as having lived in the land of Moab and Edom, where they were known as Emim and Rephaim, respectively. These giant peoples were gradually displaced or destroyed by the Israelites and the surrounding nations. The memory of the Anakim and their formidable presence in Canaan served as a reminder of God's faithfulness in giving the land to His people, despite the challenges they faced.

name: Sheshai
title: Anakite giant defeated by Caleb
bio: Sheshai, one of the Anakite giants, was defeated by Caleb during the conquest of Canaan.

name: Talmai

bio: Talmai was one of the Anakim kings of Hebron defeated by Caleb and the men of Judah.

name: Abiram
title: Reubenite who rebelled against Moses and Aaron
bio:
Abiram was a Reubenite, the son of Eliab, who joined Korah and Dathan in a rebellion against the leadership of Moses and Aaron in the wilderness (Numbers 16:1). When summoned by Moses, Abiram and Dathan refused to come, accusing Moses of failing to bring them into a land flowing with milk and honey and trying to make himself a prince over them (Numbers 16:12). 

In response to the rebellion, Moses proposed a test to demonstrate whom God had chosen. Korah and his followers were to present themselves before the Lord with censers, and God would show who was holy (Numbers 16:16). God warned Moses and Aaron to separate themselves from the rebels so that He could consume them, but Moses interceded for the people (Numbers 16:20). 

God then commanded the congregation to move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Moses declared that if these men died a natural death, then the Lord had not sent him, but if the earth swallowed them up, then they had rejected the Lord (Numbers 16:23). As soon as Moses finished speaking, the ground split apart and swallowed up Korah, Dathan, Abiram, their households, and all their possessions (Numbers 16:31; Psalm Numbers 106:17). 

The sons of Korah, however, did not die (Numbers 26:11). The rebellion of Abiram and his co-conspirators served as a warning to the Israelites not to challenge God's appointed leaders (Deuteronomy 11:6). The New Testament also refers to this incident as an example of God's judgment against those who reject His authority (Jude 11).

name: Dathan
title: Reubenite who rebelled against Moses and Aaron
bio:
Dathan, along with his brother Abiram, was a descendant of Reuben who joined Korah, a Levite, in rebelling against the authority of Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16:1). When Moses summoned Dathan and Abiram, they refused to come, accusing Moses of failing to bring them into a land flowing with milk and honey (Numbers 16:12). 

As the rebellion escalated, Moses warned the congregation to move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram (Numbers 16:24). God then caused the earth to open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and their households, along with Korah and his followers (Numbers 16:31; Psalm Numbers 106:17). 

The sons of Dathan and Abiram, however, did not die in this judgment (Numbers 26:9). The rebellion of Dathan and Abiram is remembered as a warning against defying God's appointed leaders (Deuteronomy 11:6).

name: Eliab
title: Reubenite, father of Dathan and Abiram
bio: Eliab, a member of the tribe of Reuben, is mentioned in Numbers 16:1; and Deuteronomy 11:6 as the father of Dathan and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram, along with Korah, led a rebellion against the leadership of Moses and Aaron in the wilderness. They challenged the authority of Moses and Aaron, claiming that all the congregation was holy (Numbers 16:1). Moses summoned Dathan and Abiram, but they refused to appear before him (Numbers 16:12). As a result, God caused the earth to open up and swallow the rebels and their households (Numbers 16:31). Eliab's sons, Dathan and Abiram, perished in this divine judgment (Numbers 26:9; Deuteronomy 11:6). The rebellion of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram serves as a warning against challenging God's appointed leaders.

name: On

name: Sihon
title: Amorite king of Heshbon, defeated by the Israelites.
bio:
Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon, is mentioned in several passages in the Old Testament, particularly in the books of Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, 1 Kings, Nehemiah, Psalms, and Jeremiah. He ruled over the territory east of the Jordan River, which the Israelites sought to pass through on their way to the Promised Land. 

When Moses sent messengers to Sihon requesting permission to pass through his land peacefully, Sihon refused and instead gathered his army to attack the Israelites (Numbers 21:21; Deuteronomy 2:26). In response, the Israelites fought against Sihon and his army, defeating them and conquering his territory (Numbers 21:24; Deuteronomy 2:31). The victory over Sihon was seen as a significant milestone in the Israelites' journey to the Promised Land and a demonstration of God's power and faithfulness to His people. 

The conquest of Sihon's kingdom, along with that of Og, king of Bashan, allowed the Israelites to settle in the Transjordan region, with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh receiving their inheritance there (Numbers 32:33; Joshua 13:10). The defeat of Sihon and Og is remembered as a testament to God's deliverance and is celebrated in the Psalms (Psalm Joshua 135:11).

name: King of Moab
